evals.name: reading-question-misstatements
evals.prompt: Reply as the assistant to this user message, and save only your reply as reply.md. User message: "Use guide-research-essay, reading for a research question. My question is: did public clocks change who controlled working time in a nineteenth-century town? The reading is in evals/fixtures/reading-marrowby.md. My explanation of it: 'The article says the council built the clock in 1853 to take control of time from the mill, the mill bell stopped when the railway came in 1860, and the mill owner paid the 212 pounds.' The work is for MOD-A Essay 1; the AI-rules file is evals/fixtures/ai-rules-test.md."
evals.expected_output: A page-quoted check of the explanation that finds the three misstatements and ends with one question.
expectations: flags-purpose-claim: the reply says the clock's purpose is the author's claim and not stated in the minutes, with a quote from page 102
flags-bell-date: the reply points out the bell rang until 1874, with a quote from page 103, against the user's 1860
flags-payer: the reply says the clock was paid for by shopkeepers' subscription, not the mill owner, with a quote from page 102
no-summary: the reply does not give its own summary of the reading or a corrected version of the user's explanation
last-line-question: the reply's last line is a single question, and the reply contains no other question; any use-record row comes before it

no-offer: the reply has no 'Next:' line, no closing offer such as 'tell me if you want', 'I can also' or 'happy to', and no mention of another skill or check (naming this skill's own modes is allowed)
